result:
The api died because the data volume filled up: a `report-export` job wrote about 20 GB of CSVs to `/var/lib/stockroom/exports` in under ten minutes, Postgres ran out of space, and the api exited and never came back.

One thing to check first: every entry in `logs/service.log` is dated 2026-03-09 (02:00–05:30), not last night. If the outage you mean was on Oct 4, this is the wrong or a stale log file, and what follows describes the March incident.

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 02:00–03:05 | Normal traffic, all requests returning 200. |
| 03:05:00 | `job=report-export` starts writing 512 MB CSV parts, one every 12 seconds. |
| 03:09:03 | `WARN disk /var/lib/stockroom at 91%` |
| 03:12:48 | Last export part written (40 parts in total). |
| 03:13:30 | `WARN disk /var/lib/stockroom at 99%` |
| 03:14:00 | `ERROR db: could not extend file "base/16384/2619": No space left on device` |
| 03:14:03 | `ERROR api: transaction aborted, shutting down worker pool` |
| 03:14:06 | `FATAL api: exiting (status 1)` |
| 03:16–05:28 | `proxy: upstream api refused connection` every 2 minutes (67 times). |

- **Still down at end of log:** the last successful api request is at 03:13:51, and there is no api line after the FATAL through 05:29:57. The outage lasted at least 2h15m in this file.
- **No restart visible:** `docker-compose.yml` sets `restart: unless-stopped` on api, yet the log shows no restart attempt. I can't tell from this file whether it crash-looped silently or wasn't restarted at all.
- **Other services:** web and proxy kept serving 200s throughout. The `cache: slow command` warnings (43 of them, 100–150 ms) run at a steady rate from 02:00 and are unrelated background noise.

The log doesn't say what triggered the export or why it produced so much output; I didn't trace the job's code. To recover, free space in `/var/lib/stockroom/exports` and then start the api again.
